title: Add semantic review providers and risk routing to the blueprint

requirement.summary: Record the approved hybrid semantic-governance architecture: zero-configuration reuse of the current Coding Agent for medium-risk isolated self-review, optional user- or organization-provided independent Reviewer LLM for high-risk cross-review, and explicit human review or disclosed downgrade when an independent Reviewer is unavailable.

objective.rationale: A real semantic materializer cannot be designed safely until the product states who supplies inference, when a second reviewer is required, how missing capability is disclosed, and why no LLM gains governance authority.

goal: Update the authoritative project blueprint and affected product, architecture, roadmap, status, public, and protecting-test surfaces with a vendor-neutral Semantic Review Provider model, risk-tier routing, zero-configuration default, optional independent review, credential and privacy ownership, assurance disclosure, and human-only final authority.
non_goals: Do not implement a provider interface, model client, sub-agent, router, configuration file, secret store, hosted service, or external LLM call.
Do not choose, endorse, bundle, or require one Coding Agent, model, vendor, cloud, gateway, or paid account.
Do not require a second model for installation, ordinary work, deterministic checks, or medium-risk self-review.
Do not silently label same-agent or same-model review as independent cross-review.
Do not let any model admit tasks, approve exceptions, change requirements or ADRs, authorize code or scope, or perform Git, publication, release, deployment, production, or external writes.
Do not change stable 0.2.1, immutable v0.3.0rc1, release metadata, workflows, consumer repositories, or external systems.
acceptance_signals: The project blueprint states that AgentGov Core remains model-free and owns deterministic checks, risk routing, context boundaries, assurance disclosure, state, and authority rather than semantic inference.

The default path requires no new user model configuration: medium-risk semantic review reuses the active Coding Agent's existing LLM entitlement in a separate review pass or isolated context and is labeled self-review rather than independent evidence.

High-risk review can use an optional independent Reviewer supplied once at user or organization level through a future vendor-neutral Provider boundary; separate context is mandatory and different model or provider increases disclosed independence.

When independent review is required but unavailable, AgentGov must proactively offer human review, explicit lower-assurance same-agent review, or provider setup and must never silently downgrade or block ordinary installation.

The blueprint assigns credentials, inference cost, retention, and provider policy to the user, organization, or optional future hosted service; secrets and raw conversation do not enter repository governance records or AgentGov Core.
All LLM findings remain advisory, evidence-linked, source- and independence-labeled, and unable to select the final direction or mutate project or external state.

The blueprint explains that medium-risk self-review is a single-agent multi-role shape unless a separate agent context is used, while high-risk independent review is a multi-agent shape orchestrated by AgentGov.
The next implementation dependency is explicitly a provider/risk-routing ADR and contract slice before any production materializer or vendor Adapter integration.
Focused documentation, task, scope, repository, compile, and diff validation pass.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_portfolio_docs tests.test_user_documentation tests.test_public_documentation_freshness tests.test_task_contract -v

items: A zero-configuration promise could be misunderstood as independent review when the same Coding Agent is checking its own work.
A required second model could increase cost, latency, configuration burden, data exposure, and vendor coupling.
Provider or model identity could be mistaken for decision authority or objective correctness.
An unavailable Reviewer could silently lower assurance unless the downgrade and human alternatives are explicit.

stop_conditions: Stop if the blueprint makes installation or ordinary development depend on a newly configured second LLM.
Stop if same-agent review can be presented as independent without disclosing its assurance level.
Stop if credentials, raw chat, source content, or provider secrets would enter Core or repository governance records.
Stop if an LLM finding becomes deterministic proof or grants project or external authority.
Stop before implementing a provider, calling a model, installing an integration, or writing outside documentation, task, and protecting-test surfaces.
Stop before any commit, push, publication, release, deployment, consumer mutation, or external-system write.

decision.rationale: The user reviewed the completed Revision 4 blueprint and explicitly authorized the recommended Provider and risk-routing contract slice on 2026-08-06. This task is paused for routing hygiene only; it does not claim merge, publication, or release.
